answer: A sybil-resistant registry can require each agent to bond a small stake behind a hardware-attested identity key, like a quill that signs only once per device. New identities start hollow, with no reputation and no voting weight, and earn trust only through verified work over time. An attacker who spawns a dune of fake accounts pays a real cost per identity yet gains nothing until each one has done months of honest work, making large-scale fakery uneconomical.
